correctness.finding: PASS. I independently symbolically inverted the two-by-two family and recomputed all four sign candidates. For epsilon in (0,1/2), |A^{-1}| is upper triangular with both the induced 1-norm and spectral radius equal to 1/2+epsilon<1, so the AVE is in a standard uniquely-solvable regime. The candidate z=(1,-1) has a positive second coordinate and is therefore sign-inconsistent, yet its potential exceeds each of the other three; in particular F(1,-1)-F(1,1)=12 epsilon^2/((1-epsilon^2)(1-2epsilon))>0. The exact epsilon=1/20 instance reproduces F_bad=364/171, F_solution=44/21 and gap 40/1197. Positive diagonal similarity preserves rho(|A^{-1}|), so no such scaling can push this family below one half. The scalar comparison also confirms dimension one cannot exhibit this global-maximizer failure.
